patch_description:
The current program regressed badly (0.45 vs prior 0.53). The fixed CNOT aggregators saturate entanglement before any training signal can shape the state, and CRX/CRY both mixing the same edges adds redundant parameters. 

I revert to the proven motif from the best prior ansatz (RY decoder → trainable CRY line-segment entanglers → center aggregation → center broadcast → RY/RX readout), which scored 0.53. The key improvements over that prior: (1) add a small trainable RX phase layer before the RY decoder so the circuit can shift the RX(±2π/3) feature into a more separable region before decoding (separating the three cell values requires both X and Y handling); (2) keep all entanglers parametrized (no fixed CNOTs) so the circuit starts near identity and trains smoothly under Adam. This keeps parameter count moderate and preserves the symmetric, tic-tac-toe-aware structure that generalized well (low generalization gap).
